video.title: The most expensive software bug in history...

protocol.status: v2 labeler B (rubric v2), independent of A
protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Hook: 'even before AI, software has always been held together with duct tape and the poverty of open-source maintainers.' Then the example: Knight Capital, 10% of all US stock trading, lost $440M in about 45 minutes and was sold for parts four months later (48.0). Starts on 'sometimes' to drop the leading 'But'. The recent-incidents list before it (L000-L002) is its own run-up, not needed.

The bug itself, tight enough for the band. Hook: 'deep in the codebase was an old feature flag that hadn't been used since 2003, but it was never deleted.' It triggered Power Peg, a test that buys aggressively; engineers reused the flag for new code, deployed by hand to eight servers, and only seven got the update. Payoff: the eighth server woke Power Peg from its nine-year hibernation, 'buying high and selling low' (213.0). 72s. 'At the time' and 'SMARS' are light references that the clip explains.

also_ok.why: Same story carried through the panic: they rolled back the seven healthy servers, so all eight ran Power Peg, and 45 minutes later they owned a $7B position. It is the full payoff but cannot fit 75s; the tightest cut ends on the $7B line, and the $440M / 75% drop lines (256.3) are the latest acceptable end.

negatives.why: 'In today's video... lose $10 million in a minute with this one weird trick' teaser plus the Code Report intro.

NYSE Retail Liquidity Program backstory ending in 'Just kidding, they did it in the most lazy way possible': a sarcastic line whose point needs Knight's business model from before, and it sets up the bug that comes next.
Aftermath (acquired by its competitor, absorbed in 2017) and the sarcastic 'we definitely learned our lesson', which is the sponsor segue.
Hyperagent sponsor read, which opens on a relatable joke about open-source maintainers drowning in daylight-savings issues.
